name: Mushroom Chettinad
steps: Dry-roast peppercorns, fennel, coriander seeds and chilies on low heat for 2–3 minutes. Add coconut for the final minute; cool and grind with 70 ml water to a coarse paste.
Wipe mushrooms dry and halve. Heat oil in a wide pan; sauté mushrooms 5 minutes until their moisture evaporates, then remove.
In the same pan, fry curry leaves 20 seconds and onion 6 minutes until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and stir 1 minute; add tomato and salt and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in coarse spice-coconut paste and remaining 80 ml water. Cook 5 minutes, stirring, until dark and aromatic; return mushrooms and toss well.
Simmer 3 minutes until mushrooms are coated in the thick peppery masala. Serve hot with rice or chapati.
tips: Black pepper and roasted coconut should lead the flavor; avoid making it a generic tomato gravy.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
